items.title: Mauritania Poverty and Equity Brief : October 2026
items.summary: In 2026, rising inflation and weak agricultural growth are expected to increase moderate poverty at the lower-middle-income poverty line of US$4.20 per person per day (2021 PPP) to 24.1 percent, pushing an estimated 60,000 additional Mauritanians into poverty. The extreme poverty rate is expected to increase to 9.7 percent. While the moderate poverty rate declined from 26.5 percent in 2020 to 23.6 percent in 2025, progress has been limited and is expected to reverse. This reflects a growth model driven largely by capital-intensive extractive industries, which generates limited direct benefits…

items.title: Dietary diversity among women of reproductive age (15–49 yrs) across rural and urban settings: a scoping review
items.summary: Dietary diversity (DD) reflects micronutrient adequacy and diet quality. Inadequate dietary diversity has adverse effects on health of the women and increases the risk of complications during pregnancy and childbirth due to deficiencies of micronutrients. This scoping review aims to synthesize the current understanding of dietary diversity among WRA in urban and rural settings, highlighting key findings from recent studies. A thorough literature search using electronic databases such as Scopus, PubMed and Google Scholar was conducted. Published articles between 2014 and 2025 were included.…

items.summary: This sampling survey was designed to rapidly measure the protection and socio-economic impact of COVID-19 on the refugee population in Mbera camp the region of Hodh Echargui in Mauritania. items.title: Africa - Monthly and dekadal combined drought indicator (CDI)

items.title: Zenaga Reflexes of Berber Final Weak Verbs
items.summary: Berber languages outside Mauritania have a number of different morphological classes of vowel-final and semivowel-final verbs (“final weak verbs”). The situation in Zenaga of Mauritania looks very different. In this article, the Zenaga reflexes of the non- Mauritanian weak verbs are compared by studying all relevant cognates. As a result, it proves possible to establish to what extent the main weak verb classes of non- Mauritanian Berber are reflected in Zenaga, and to what extent certain irregularities can be understood from Zenaga-internal developments.

items.summary: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).

items.summary: El Sáhara Occidental continúa siendo un territorio no autónomo, pendiente de descolonización y bajo supervisión de la ONU. Desde 1976, Marruecos ocupa gran parte del territorio, sin reconocimiento de soberanía por parte del Derecho Internacional. España, antigua potencia administradora, abandonó la zona sin cumplir el compromiso de celebrar un referendo de autodeterminación. Tradicionalmente, las soluciones planteadas han sido la independencia o la integración en Marruecos con un régimen de autonomía. items.title: Modélisation hydrodynamique et morpho-dynamique du transport sédimentaire sur les côtes sahéliennes : application au littoral de Nouakchott
items.summary: Les littoraux sableux du Sahel se caractérisent par une dynamique hydro-sédimentaire particulièrement intense. items.title: A new species of Thelepus (Annelida, Terebelliformia) from Banc d’Arguin, Mauritania, and its associated scaleworm Lepidonotus hupferi Augener, 1918 (Annelida, Polynoidae)
items.summary: To date, only one species of the terebellid polychaete genus Thelepus Leuckart, 1849 has been described from Africa: T. pequenianus Augener, 1918. items.summary: Depuis les années 2000, le développement des industries de transformation et de conditionnement du poisson en Afrique du nord-ouest a favorisé l’accès de plusieurs centaines de femmes à l’emploi salarié dans un secteur historiquement masculin. Cette dynamique a contribué à transformer la configuration socioprofessionnelle de la filière halieutique en Mauritanie, notamment dans les villes côtières de Nouadhibou et de Nouakchott.
